documents.prompt: The generated data include $(0,{{y0}})$. Use linear-regression technology to WRITE the fitted function $y=mx+b$, then predict $y$ when $x=6$.

solutionReview.headline: Regression produces the equation before the prediction.
reasoning: Use linear regression on all five points and record both the slope and intercept in $y=mx+b$.
Substitute the requested input into that fitted equation, then decide whether the prediction is interpolation or extrapolation.

attemptFeedback: Do not predict until you have written both regression coefficients.
supportHints: Use all data points in the regression; a line through only two selected points is not the requested fitted model.

variants.prompt: Use linear regression technology on all SEVEN noisy observations to WRITE the best-fit function y=mx+b, then use that fitted model to predict the response at x=10. Do not replace regression with a line through two selected points.

context.title: Seven-observation linear regression
context.note: The target x=10 is outside the observed range 0 through 6.

solutionReview.headline: More observations and a farther target increase computational/structural difficulty without changing the reasoning level.
reasoning: Run linear regression on all seven observations and record both fitted coefficients.
Use the fitted equation—not a two-point line—to evaluate the model at x=10.
Because x=10 lies beyond the observed range, the numerical result is an extrapolation.
solutionReview.answerSummary: Write the regression line and its x=10 prediction.

attemptFeedback: Use all seven pairs in the regression list before evaluating x=10.
